title: Five Things We’ve Learned About Barcelona Ahead of November International Break
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas5:00 PM ESTBarcelona are off to their best start of the season of the Hansi Flick era—but there’s still plenty of room for improvement.  / Thomas Coex/AFP/Getty ImagesThe final international break of 2026 arrives with Barcelona sitting atop the La Liga standings, inside the top eight in the Champions League league phase and on a high after a massive victory at Atlético Madrid. Yet, things aren’t as rose-colored as they were a month and a half ago.

Barcelona won six of the eight games they played between the two fall international windows, continuing to score in bunches, asserting themselves as one of Europe’s most dangerous teams and improving their season record to 14 wins from 16.

But the flaws of Hansi Flick’s side were also exposed. Barcelona’s perfect season came to an end at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain and then fell at home against a surging Real Madrid only days later in the first El Clásico of the campaign.

Although Barcelona rebounded and won three straight before the break—including the gargantuan victory against Atlético—defeats in the two biggest games of the season and a significant injury crisis have slightly dampened the mood on the season.

The two-week break will certainly help Barcelona recover players from injury and give Flick time to analyze where his team can improve entering a busy period of the campaign. With a quarter of the season in the rearview mirror, here’s five things we learned about Barcelona over their last eight games.

Barcelona came back to reality after a flawless start of the season.  / Jose Hernandez/Anadolu/Getty ImagesAfter winning their opening 11 games of 2026–27, Barcelona received two major reality checks against PSG and Real Madrid that bursted their fairytale bubble. The Catalans are not the best team in the world—PSG remain the team to beat—and they’ll have to continue improving or Real Madrid could seriously challenge their La Liga crown.

It’s not just that Barcelona’s record through 11 games was perfect; it’s that they were demolishing opponents. As a result, a sense of invincibility bled into Flick’s Barça 3.0, but two defeats and some shaky stretches during games decidedly removed any notion that the Catalans can’t be defeated.
Barcelona are mortal, with weakness strong opponents can exploit. Despite their strong start to the campaign, they haven’t won anything yet.

Still, coming back to reality doesn’t mean Barcelona are no longer contenders for major silverware. In fact, facing some adversity with the season still in its first half should help the team in the long run.

Lamine Yamal (left) and Raphinha have become an unstoppable force.  / Julian Finney/Getty ImagesIf Barcelona are going to have a chance of lifting their third straight league title and ending their 11-year Champions League drought, Lamine Yamal and Raphinha will likely be the biggest reasons why.
The attackers proved their incredible start to the season wasn’t just a purple patch and have continued to be incredibly productive in the aftermath of the September–October international break.

Both players are currently on 18 goal contributions in La Liga, the most of any player in the division. Raphinha leads the Pichichi race with 15 goals and Yamal is up to 25 goal contributions for Barça this season—the most of any player in Europe’s top five leagues.
Even when they aren’t playing their best games, they remain incredibly productive, evidenced by Raphinha’s strike against Real Madrid and Yamal’s moment of magic against PSG.

Barcelona’s route to success will come down to them outscoring opponents, and with Yamal and Raphinha at this level, they’ll have a chance against anyone. Add Fermín López’s 15 goal contributions into the mix and you have a prolific trio.

Frenkie de Jong has been brilliant since returning from injury.  / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesBarcelona acquiring Rodri after a sensational World Cup campaign for Spain came only weeks after Frenkie de Jong suffered a knee injury during said tournament.

The Dutchman was harshly criticized for playing the World Cup on an injured knee and with Rodri joining the club, many believed De Jong’s time at Barcelona could be coming to an end. But after missing the first two months of the campaign, De Jong is back and through four appearances, he’s emphatically silenced his critics.

Whether it’s at center back, right back or midfield, De Jong hasn’t put a foot wrong since returning from injury. His introduction in the second half against Atlético Madrid completely changed the game, as Barcelona were able to assume control of the match and eventually cruise to the finish line, with him and Pedri taking over the game.

De Jong and Pedri have barely played together in 2026, but they’ve formed a stellar partnership since Flick’s arrival. The Dutchman is making a strong case to keep his place in the XI even once Rodri returns from injury.

If all three are healthy, Flick turning to a 4-3-3 formation with a midfield trio of Rodri, Pedri and De Jong should be in consideration. But seemingly for the millionth time, the Dutchman has proven he belongs in Barça’s strongest XI.
